## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sīlaṁnacittānuparivattītikathā* (Kv 10.8) is the eighth discourse of the tenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the third treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text deals with whether virtue or bodily discipline conforms to or follows thought (*citta*), which S. N. Dube classifies in secondary literature as one of the psycho-ethical controversies recorded in the *Kathāvatthu* [Dube 1980]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral does not record any curated parallels for the text [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal connections across 14 canonical and paracanonical works (comprising 138 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Its largest shared passages occur with related doctrinal discussions within the *Kathāvatthu*, specifically *Sīlaṁacetasikantikathā* (Kv 10.7), *Rūpaṁkammantikathā* (Kv 8.9), and *Rūpaṁmaggotikathā* (Kv 10.2), as well as the commentary *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and canonical Abhidhamma works such as the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (both its *Mātikā* and *Rūpavibhatti*), *Paṭṭhāna*, and *Vibhaṅga* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments calculated by DharmaNexus suggest shared phrasing or doctrinal lists with Sanskrit sources—notably Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha* and the *Mahāvyutpatti*—as well as Tibetan canonical and commentarial texts including the *Arthaviniścayaṭīkā*, *Karmasiddhiṭīkā*, and *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* [DharmaNexus].
